title: Weird and mysterious words stories vs retro computing stories on comments
question: Does a story about weird and mysterious words get more comments than a story about retro computing?
author: film-cards
hypothesis: A story about weird and mysterious words gets more comments than a story about retro computing.
expect: If true, comments per story for weird and mysterious words stories should be at least 1.5x the value for retro computing stories, over all stories from 2006 to 2026 (1.1x is weak, 0.9x or lower refutes it).

check.per_label: comments per story, weird and mysterious words against retro computing

group_a.label: Weird and mysterious words stories ({from} to {to})

thresholds_note: Thresholds are the ones used on h370, set before this card was run and not tuned to its result. h356 is left unchanged.
caveats: Points are the score each story had when the archive fetched it, so 2025 and 2026 stories may still be gaining points.
A title that names a theme is not proof the story is about it, and one story can sit in both groups.
Both groups are title words only, so stories that never name the theme are missed.
h356 asked a different question; this card compares two groups head to head.
